title: Affine-chart compact localization with the actual restriction map
statement: Let k₀ be finite and l a prime different from its characteristic. Let X,Y be k₀-schemes and π:Y→X a separated quasi-compact morphism locally of finite type over k₀. Suppose (π,s):Y→X×_{k₀}A¹ is a cartesian presentation, and X is locally of finite type, quasi-compact and quasi-separated over k₀. With G and ρ of [def-pur-b3-weil-projective-restriction], there is a natural α:π*⋙Rπ_!→G such that for every native Weil complex K, some connecting arrow w makes Rπ_!π*K --α_K→ G(K) --ρ_K→ K --w→ (Rπ_!π*K)[1] a distinguished triangle. Neither the proper projective-line decomposition nor the invertibility of an affine integration map is asserted.

source.place: Apply proper direct image to the canonical affine-chart/infinity localization triangle

proof.text: The given cartesian square identifies Y over X with A¹_X. The standard affine chart of P¹_X compactifies this projection, with complementary closed section infinity; the formulas and range-complement identity are those of [sk-d-lines]. This geometry works over arbitrary, including nonreduced, X.

For q* K on P¹_X, take the canonical open counit and the closed unit of [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]. Apply proper direct image, which preserves distinguished triangles. Use the proper shriek/star comparison and composition comparison to identify the three terms with Rπ_!π*K, Rq_*q*K, and K. These identifications are natural in K. The first arrow therefore gives a natural transformation α into the middle functor. The existing native objectwise localization theorem supplies the same vertex pattern; the extra requirement here is to retain the actual canonical second arrow through these comparisons.

The second arrow is the restriction of cohomology to infinity. Transpose the closed unit, apply the proper-composition comparison, and cancel i≫q=id. Counit naturality and the two adjunction identities identify the resulting map with e⁻¹ at Rq_*q*K followed by i* of the q-counit and then e at K. This is precisely the constructed ρ of [def-pur-b3-weil-projective-restriction]. Transporting the distinguished triangle along the natural vertex comparisons proves the assertion, with no claim about cohomology of the proper or affine line.
